title: Methods to Mitigate Escherichia coli Blooms in Ex Vivo Colon Model Experiments
author: Mathur, Mechoud, et al.

steps.title: Obtain approval and collect fecal samples
steps.instruction: Seek ethical approval to collect faecal samples from 6–10 volunteers (preferably on multiple occasions) and collect each sample in sterile faecal pots.

substeps.instruction: Store collected pots at 4 °C (no longer than 3 h) in anaerobic gas jars with Anaerocult® A gas packs.
Keep pots in the anaerobic chamber at 37 °C for pooling and processing once all volunteers have contributed.

steps.title: Pool and process fecal material for FSI
steps.instruction: Weigh equal amounts of each sample to obtain a total of 400 g pooled faeces (e.g., 40 g from each of 10 volunteers).

substeps.instruction: Place pooled faeces into a sterile stomacher bag containing a sieve (e.g., Seward Stomacher® bag) inside the anaerobic chamber.
Add 400 ml of 50 mM phosphate buffer containing 0.05 % w/v L‑cysteine‑HCl, hand‑mix for 2 min to obtain a homogeneous slurry.
Separate solid and liquid by sieving; collect the liquid slurry into 50 ml conical Falcon tubes.

steps.title: Centrifuge and reconstitute fecal pellets
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Falcon tubes at 4000 g for 25 min at ambient temperature (~18 °C).

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in its original starting volume using sterile 50 mM phosphate buffer with 0.05 % w/v L‑cysteine‑HCl and 25 % (v/v) glycerol.

steps.title: Aliquot and freeze standardized inoculum
steps.instruction: Pool all resuspended suspensions into a sterile bottle, invert 3–4 times to mix, and aliquot 12 ml into sterile 15 ml Falcon tubes.

substeps.instruction: Store aliquots at –80 °C; each aliquot constitutes a frozen standardised inoculum (FSI) for one downstream micro‑Matrix experiment.

steps.title: Prepare anaerobic chamber and micro‑Matrix components
steps.instruction: Ensure the anaerobic chamber is strictly anaerobic before any work.

substeps.instruction: Place a resazurin indicator strip inside the chamber to confirm anaerobiosis.
Verify supply of anaerobic gas mix (10 % CO₂, 10 % H₂ in N₂) and technical‑grade nitrogen cylinders for the chamber.
Confirm sufficient BIPR nitrogen and CO₂ cylinders for the micro‑Matrix unit.

steps.title: Autoclave and dry top plate and filter bars
steps.instruction: Autoclave the micro‑Matrix top plate at 121 °C for 15 min in an autoclave bag.

substeps.instruction: If filter bars are to be reused, autoclave them in a beaker covered with tin foil at 121 °C for 15 min.
After autoclaving, dry the top plate and all four filter bars in a laminar‑flow hood for 2 h until completely moisture‑free.

steps.title: Assemble filter bars and pre‑equilibrate supplies
steps.instruction: Under aseptic conditions in a laminar‑flow hood, assemble the four sterile filter bars onto the dried top plate, checking for perfect hermetic seals.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑equilibrate all plasticware, reagents and other materials in the anaerobic chamber overnight.
Ensure liquid ammonia (20 % v/v) for pH control is ≤4 weeks old and available in sufficient volume.

steps.title: Prepare Faecal Fermentation Medium (FFM) solution
steps.instruction: Prepare double‑strength FFM according to Table 1 (multiply each listed concentration by two).

substeps.instruction: Tryptone 2000 mg/L ×2, Yeast extract 2000 mg/L ×2, Cysteine‑HCl 1000 mg/L ×2, Bile salts 500 mg/L ×2, NaHCO₃ 2000 mg/L ×2, Tween 80 2 ml/L ×2, Hemin 50 µl/L ×2, Vitamin K₁ 10 µl/L ×2, NaCl 1 ml/L ×2, KH₂PO₄ 1 ml/L ×2, K₂HPO₄ 1 ml/L ×2, CaCl₂·6H₂O 1 ml/L ×2, MgSO₄·7H₂O 1 ml/L ×2.
Autoclave the prepared medium before use.

steps.title: Pre‑equilibrate substrates and thaw FSI
steps.instruction: Introduce test substrates into the anaerobic chamber at least 2 h before the experiment (or overnight for non‑microbial substrates).

substeps.instruction: Thaw one 12 ml FSI aliquot in the chamber for a maximum of 15 min.

steps.title: Mix FSI with double‑strength FFM and add test substrate
steps.instruction: Combine 12 ml thawed FSI with 80 ml double‑strength FFM and mix gently.

substeps.instruction: Dispense an arbitrary volume (e.g., 10 ml) of this FSI/FFM mixture into sterile universal Sterilin tubes.
Add an equal volume of the test substrate to each tube (for negative controls, add sterile, anaerobically pre‑equilibrated water).
Invert the tubes 3–4 times to mix.

steps.title: Dispense mixtures into bioreactor wells
steps.instruction: Pipette 7 ml of each prepared sample into the designated wells of the micro‑Matrix cassette.

steps.title: Take initial (T0) sample from each well
steps.instruction: Before the first time‑point sampling, homogenise each well by pipetting 1 ml up and down three times.

substeps.instruction: Collect two 1 ml aliquots for downstream analyses (DNA, metabolomics, proteomics, etc.).
Leave ~5 ml of liquid in each well to start the fermentation.

steps.title: Seal cassette and install on micro‑Matrix unit
steps.instruction: Place the pre‑assembled top plate with filter bars onto the cassette, ensuring a perfectly hermetic seal.

substeps.instruction: Visually confirm that the top plate and clamps are straight and aligned.
Remove the sealed cassette from the anaerobic chamber and mount it onto the micro‑Matrix unit, attaching the gas bars to the four rows.

steps.title: Start fermentation with defined parameters
steps.instruction: Initiate the run using the software with the following set points:

substeps.instruction: Dissolved oxygen (DO): 0–150 % air saturation (lower/upper limits).
pH: target 6.8, limits 6.2–7.2.
Temperature: 37 °C, limits 35–39 °C.
Orbital shaking: 275 rpm.
Activate liquid ammonia flow within 1 min of start.

steps.title: Monitor parameters and adjust gases during run
steps.instruction: Continuously record real‑time DO, pH, temperature, and dosage rates of BIPR nitrogen, CO₂ and liquid ammonia, checking at regular intervals.

steps.title: Pause fermentation and sample at designated time points
steps.instruction: When required (e.g., T6 hr, T24 hr), pause the run and repeat the sampling procedure described for T0.

substeps.instruction: Disassemble the top plate and cassette as needed, take aliquots, then re‑seal and resume fermentation.

steps.title: Terminate experiment, collect final samples, save data
steps.instruction: At the end of the run, remove the cassette, take final aliquots using the same method as for T0, and complete the instrument checklists to save raw parameter data.

substeps.instruction: Switch off all gases (BIPR nitrogen, CO₂, liquid ammonia) and close associated valves.

steps.title: Apply INFOGEST digestion, dialysis, and lyophilisation to substrates
steps.instruction: Digest test substrates according to the static INFOGEST protocol, then dialyse to reduce small‑molecule content.

substeps.instruction: Place digested substrate in 500 Da dialysis tubing and dialyse for 24–30 h with four water changes, immersing the tubing in ~100 × its volume (e.g., 30 ml substrate in 3 L distilled water).
Allow for osmotic swelling; adjust external water volume accordingly to maintain the gradient.
After dialysis (≈10‑fold dilution), lyophilise the sample to remove excess water.
Re‑constitute the lyophilised powder in the original starting volume with sterile distilled water before adding to the micro‑Matrix experiment.

description:
Experiments involving the use of ex vivo colon models are regularly conducted with a view to assessing the impact of a variety of substrates, nutrients, drugs, antimicrobials, amongst other substances on the gut microbiome. The micro-Matrix bioreactor fermentation system (Applikon) is an example of a platform that can be employed to undertake such experiments. However, researchers using this system often encounter Escherichia coli blooms. Herein we report the complex combination of factors that contribute to E. coli blooms in such experiments. More specifically, we list these causative factors, provide evidence to support their description as causative factors, and share insights gained from our troubleshooting efforts with a view to attenuating such blooms. Examples of such factors include the prolonged storage of the frozen standardised inoculum (FSI) faecal slurry at −80 °C, the presence of simple sugars such as glucose in the substrates tested, the broader composition of the substrates/samples tested as well as the concentration of dissolved oxygen (DO) present during the ex vivo colon model experiment. Overall, we describe and outline revised optimised standard operating procedures (SOPs) and appropriate steps with a view to attenuating E. coli blooms (Fig. 1), specifically when using the micro-Matrix bioreactor fermentation platform as an ex vivo model of the human distal colon.Fig. 1Flow chart depicting the main steps involved in ex vivo colon model experiments where our recommended optimisations are critical to mitigate E. coli blooms.Fig 1 1. Recommended optimised method for frozen standardised inoculum (FSI) preparation (derived and adapted from O'Donnell et al. 2016)

), to minimise downstream E. coli blooms:
○Seek ethical approval to collect faecal samples from a cohort of 6–10 volunteers. We strongly recommend seeking approval to collect faecal samples on multiple occasions to avoid the need to store FSI for prolonged periods.○Collect faecal samples
